gaps.sentence: We're looking forward to ___ from you soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Look forward to + -ing' — 'to' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: It's not worth ___ about the delay — nothing will change.
I can't imagine ___ in a tiny village again.
We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).

gaps.sentence: I was made ___ the dustbin lorry at six in the morning.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, make takes the to-infinitive: was made to wait.

gaps.sentence: They managed ___ the fire before it spread.
gaps.explanation: manage takes the to-infinitive: managed to put out.

gaps.sentence: I'd rather you ___ smoke in here.
gaps.explanation: would rather + somebody + past simple: I'd rather you didn't smoke.
